extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) staff handling inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners on choosing, drafting, and processing Office actions (including non-ACP actions and Actions Closing Prosecution) and on panel review and post-ACP submissions in inter partes reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining next Office action based on responses and third-party comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner selects the next Office action based on whether the patent owner timely responded and whether third party requester comments were timely provided (covers cases A–D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely patent owner response, third party comments cannot be filed. If patent owner responded but third party did not, follow incomplete/formality/ACP paths as applicable. If both responded, apply same set of checks (incomplete, formality, out-of-scope comments), and issue ACP only when proceeding is ready. See MPEP § 2671.01 for subcases and references to §§ 2666.30, 2666.50, 2672, and 2673.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-response: Issue Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) when all claims under rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to timely respond and all claims are under rejection, the examiner will issue a Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims will be canceled by formal examiner’s amendment (attached as part of the NIRC). No panel review conference is needed in this instance, as issuance of the NIRC is essentially ministerial. See MPEP § 2687.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-response: Issue Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) when at least one claim patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner does not respond and at least one claim is free of rejection/objection, issue an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) limiting the proceeding to those patentable claims and to claims added or amended which do not expand scope of the patentable claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACP will state that claims under rejection/objection are withdrawn from consideration and will be canceled upon issuance of an NIRC; see MPEP § 2666.10 for entry of new claims that do not expand scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may issue supplemental Office action if new information warrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when there has been no patent owner response, the examiner is free to issue a supplemental Office action providing a new rejection where new information comes to attention warranting the new rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an action would ordinarily not be made an ACP. New grounds not previously addressed normally prevent closing prosecution unless necessitated by an amendment (37 CFR 1.949).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete response => Issue incomplete-response action
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner’s response is incomplete, the examiner may issue an incomplete-response action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2666.30 for procedures and form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality defect in patent owner response => Notice of Defective Paper in Reexam
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a formality defect in the patent owner’s response, the examiner will issue a Notice of Defective Paper in Reexam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2666.50 for specifics on identifying the defect and giving opportunity to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party comments beyond permitted scope => treat as improper comments
rubrics_metrics.description: If third party requester comments go beyond what is permitted, the examiner will follow procedures for improper comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2666.05 to handle comments that exceed permitted scope (e.g., out-of-scope argumentation or evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: When an Office action will not close prosecution (non-ACP issuance criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: An action will not normally close prosecution if it includes a new ground of rejection not previously addressed by the patent owner, unless necessitated by an amendment; examiner may also issue a non-ACP when issues are not clearly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the patent owner’s right to amend claims prior to closure. Examiner discretion to issue a non-ACP is appropriate when more development or clarification of issues is needed (see 37 CFR 1.949 and MPEP § 2671.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall content requirements for non-ACP Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-ACP Office action should be comprehensive, addressing all issues raised by the patent owner’s response and third-party comments and be a statement of the examiner’s position complete enough so the next action can properly be an ACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action must clearly set forth each ground of rejection and/or objection and the supporting reasons; for each third-party-proposed rejection the examiner refuses to adopt, the reasons why that rejection is not appropriate must be clearly stated; provide comprehensive reasons for patentability where favorable (see MPEP § 1302.14 for examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of amendatory matter under 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment has been submitted, the amendatory matter (revised or newly added matter) should be reviewed for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112; the unamended patent content should not be reviewed under 112 in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review limited to newly presented or revised text only; do not perform a full 112 review of unchanged patent disclosure during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of a rejection must be clearly stated as favorable to patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner withdraws a ground of rejection originally initiated by the examiner, that withdrawal should be clearly stated in the Office action as a decision favorable to patentability with respect to the withdrawn rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawn rejection was originally proposed by third party and claims were not amended, treat as a third-party-proposed rejection that the examiner refuses to adopt and state reasons. If withdrawn rejections relate to amended claims, normally they are not treated as refusals to adopt since the original rejection was not proposed against amended claims; explain treatment and appellate consequences (37 CFR 41.61(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and note issues not within scope of inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If issues not within scope (e.g., public use, on-sale, conduct, abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102) are raised, the examiner will note existence of such questions in the Office action using form paragraph 26.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form ¶26.03 should identify the issues in bracket 1 and state the issue will not be considered in the present proceeding (37 CFR 1.906(c)). Such issues should not be raised independently by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet and response period requirements for Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Form PTOL-2064 as the Office action cover sheet for non-ACP actions and PTOL-2065 for ACPs; fill in the space for the date(s) of the communication(s) the Office action responds to and the default response period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, non-ACP actions give the patent owner two months to respond (insert 'Two'); ACPs give one month (insert 'One') or 30 days/one month (whichever is longer) as appropriate. Ensure proper form used and fields populated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority: primary examiner must sign actions on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: All Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding must be signed by a primary examiner (including non-ACP and ACP actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to all substantive communications in the proceeding to ensure proper authority and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding paragraphs should caution patent owner about complete responses and 37 CFR 1.116(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions should include concluding language warning the patent owner that a complete response should be made since the next action may be an ACP and that 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced after an ACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert form paragraph 26.05 followed by form paragraph 26.73 at the end of the Office action. Explain that after an ACP any amendment must include a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they are necessary and were not earlier presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers to be submitted in response to Office action must be submitted in response (timeliness of amendments/evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure full consideration of amendments, affidavits/declarations, or other evidence of patentability, such documents must be submitted in response to this Office action; submissions after the next Office action (expected to be an ACP) will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116(b) and (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions filed after the next Office action risk strict limitation or exclusion; emphasize early presentation of evidence under 37 CFR 1.131(a) or 1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence channels and EFS-Web timeliness and certificate requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence should be directed to the CRU using specified channels (EFS-Web, mail, fax, hand delivery); for EFS-Web transmissions, timeliness requires compliance with 37 CFR 1.6(a)(4) and inclusion of a certificate of transmission stating the date of transmission prior to expiration of the response period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide addresses/contacts (PTOL/EFS-Web link, mail stop, fax numbers, telephone) and note that except for certain requests, correspondence transmitted via EFS-Web with proper certificate is considered timely under 37 CFR 1.8(a)(1)(i)(C) and (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for preparing the Office action and panel setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of responses (or expiration of response time), the examiner will be notified and will prepare for and set up a panel review conference per MPEP § 2671.03 to discuss issuance of the Office action; the examiner may prepare the action before or after the conference and revise as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision to reject/allow, the proposed Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner with two or more conferees initialing the action to indicate presence. If conference does not confirm, the examiner must reevaluate and issue appropriate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: No response by patent owner and claims patentable: issue ACP and limit proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to respond to an action and claims have been found patentable, the examiner will issue an ACP which repeats determinations of patentability and limits the proceeding to the claims found patentable and to new claims which do not expand scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACP should incorporate by reference reasons for determinations and include more explanation if helpful. A panel review conference will be held per MPEP § 2671.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACP content and characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACP must set forth all rejections and determinations not to make a proposed rejection and the grounds therefor; ACPs are not final actions (cannot be appealed) and their criteria are analogous to making a rejection final in an application (MPEP § 706.07(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACP should be clearly developed so the patent owner and third party may judge whether to file comments under 37 CFR 1.951. ACP may incorporate previous complete statements by reference but must include rebuttals to patent owner arguments and consider third-party comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling prior art cited by patent owner during prosecution (IDS submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where art is submitted in a prior art citation (an IDS) and not accompanied by a 37 CFR 1.97(e)-type statement, the examiner may use the art and make the next Office action an ACP whether or not claims have been amended, provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced based on art not cited in the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(a) regarding making rejection final when relying on newly submitted art; the IDS in reexamination is construed as a prior art citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review will consist of three members: a manager (one member), the examiner in charge of the proceeding (second), and a manager-selected third member. Examiner-conferees should be primary examiners or examiners knowledgeable in the technology and/or experienced in reexamination practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority of those present should be examiners not involved in original examination or issuance of the patent. An original examiner should be chosen only if most knowledgeable or for other specific justifiable reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel process mechanics and initialing
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner informs the manager of intent to issue an Office action; the manager convenes a panel to confer and review patentability; if conference confirms preliminary decision, the Office action is issued and signed by the examiner with the two conferees initialing the action as 'conferee' to indicate participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both conferees initial even if one dissented. If the conference does not confirm the preliminary decision, the examiner reevaluates; if the examiner in charge disagrees with conference decision, the manager generally assigns the proceeding to another examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel objectives: comprehensive review and reduce perceived bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Each conference should provide a forum to consider all issues of patentability and procedural issues impacting patentability, with review by more than one primary examiner to diminish perceptions of undue influence and to ensure all matters are properly addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel should detect issues the examiner in charge might have missed and provide comprehensive discussion and findings on each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and remedy if a panel review is not held
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is issued without a panel review, the patent owner or third party requester wishing to object must promptly file a paper alerting the Office; any challenge must be made within two weeks of receipt or will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to hold a panel review will be apparent by absence of conferees’ initials. However, failure to hold a conference by itself is not grounds for vacating Office decisions or restarting the reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: One opportunity to make submissions after ACP under 37 CFR 1.951(a) and (b)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an ACP the patent owner may once file written comments limited to issues raised and/or a proposed amendment (subject to 37 CFR 1.116); when patent owner files comments, the third party may once file comments responsive under 37 CFR 1.951(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any second or supplemental submission after ACP by either party will be returned. Third party comments must be filed within 30 days from service of the patent owner’s submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for patent owner submission under 37 CFR 1.951(a) and limits on extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner submissions under 1.951(a) must be filed within the response period set in the ACP (normally 30 days or one month). Extensions may be requested under 37 CFR 1.956 but may not extend past six months from the ACP date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and parties should recognize reexamination may result in final cancellation of claims and therefore should identify and develop all issues prior to the ACP, including early presentation of evidence under 37 CFR 1.131(a) or 1.132.
